agents.description: Software architect subagent that designs a new system or module, or evaluates an existing one, by pinning down constraints and quality attributes, comparing two or three concrete options on their trade-offs, and returning one recommendation with risks and a migration path, all without editing code. Use when the user asks how a system should be structured, wants a monolith, microservice, queue or datastore choice weighed, or wants an independent assessment of whether the current design will hold up.

agents.name: code-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews a diff or branch for correctness bugs in a separate context and returns a short, verified list of findings ranked by severity, without editing any files. Use when the user asks for a code review of their changes, a second pair of eyes before a commit or pull request, or a check of whether a change breaks existing callers.

agents.name: code-simplifier
agents.description: Cleans up freshly written or recently modified code by flattening deep nesting, collapsing pointless wrappers and indirection, removing duplicated logic and clarifying names, while keeping behaviour identical and confirming it with the existing test suite. Use when the user asks to tidy, simplify or make more readable the code they just wrote or the files touched in the current diff or last few commits.

agents.name: cpp-build-resolver
agents.description: Gets a broken C++ build green again by diagnosing compiler errors, linker failures such as undefined reference or LNK2019, CMake configure problems, and vcpkg or Conan dependency issues, then applying the smallest fix and rebuilding to prove it. Use when a C++ project fails to configure, compile or link, CMake cannot find a package, symbols are missing or duplicated, or a dependency manager upgrade broke the build.

agents.name: cpp-reviewer
agents.description: C++ change reviewer that hunts for undefined behaviour, dangling references and views, use-after-move, memory and handle leaks, data races, broken exception safety and ABI breaks in public headers, then returns ranked, verified findings without editing code. Use when a C++ diff, branch or pull request needs a review before merge, or when the user suspects a memory-safety, lifetime or threading bug in changed C++ code.

agents.name: csharp-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing .NET builds by reading dotnet restore and dotnet build output and fixing C# compiler errors, NuGet restore failures, package downgrades and version conflicts, target framework and SDK mismatches, and analyzer warnings treated as errors, using the smallest diff and re-running the build to prove it. Use when dotnet build, dotnet restore or dotnet test will not compile, a NuGet NU1xxx error blocks restore, or an SDK or TargetFramework upgrade broke the solution.

agents.name: csharp-reviewer
agents.description: C# and .NET change reviewer that hunts for async void, sync-over-async deadlocks, nullable-safety holes, undisposed resources, repeated LINQ enumeration, EF Core query mistakes and DI lifetime bugs, then returns verified findings ranked by severity without touching files. Use when a C# diff, branch or pull request needs a .NET-specific bug review before it merges, or when a .NET service hangs, leaks or throws NullReferenceException after a recent change.

agents.name: dart-build-resolver
agents.description: Gets a red Dart or Flutter build back to green with the smallest diff, resolving dart analyze and flutter analyze errors, compile failures, pub "version solving failed" dependency conflicts and build_runner code generation problems (stale or conflicting .g.dart and .freezed.dart outputs, missing part directives, generator and analyzer version clashes), then re-runs the failing command to prove it passes. Use when dart or flutter analyze, flutter build, dart compile, pub get or build_runner is failing and the user wants it fixed.

agents.name: dart-reviewer
agents.description: Dart-language bug hunter for diffs in packages, CLIs, servers and the logic layers of Flutter apps (repositories, blocs, services), checking `!` and `late` null-safety escapes, unawaited or discarded futures, StreamSubscription and StreamController leaks, isolate and port misuse, non-exhaustive sealed switches, plus setState after dispose and side effects in build methods where widgets are touched; it verifies each finding and returns a severity-ranked list without editing files. Use when a Dart diff, branch or pull request needs checking for async, stream and null-safety bugs before merge, rather than a Flutter UI review of rebuilds and platform behaviour.

agents.name: database-reviewer
agents.description: Database change auditor for SQL schema files, migrations, ORM models and query code, checking for DDL that takes blocking table locks, unindexed filters and foreign keys, N+1 query loops, destructive or irreversible migrations that can lose data, and transaction bugs such as read-then-write races or missing rollbacks, and returning verified findings by severity without changing anything. Use when a pull request touches migrations, schema or database queries, before running a migration on a large production table, or when the user asks whether a query or data model change is safe.

agents.name: django-reviewer
agents.description: Django-focused reviewer that inspects a diff or branch for N+1 querysets, raw SQL built from user input, views and DRF endpoints missing authentication or object-level permission checks, migrations that lock or break live tables, and insecure or environment-leaking settings, then returns verified, severity-ranked findings without modifying files. Use when someone wants Django models, views, serializers, migrations or settings checked before merge or deploy.

agents.name: doc-updater
agents.description: Brings documentation back in line with a code change by reading the diff, finding every README, docs page, docstring, code comment, example and changelog entry that now describes old behaviour, and editing only those documentation files so they match the new code. Use when a change renamed, added or removed a flag, endpoint, config key or function and the docs need syncing, or before a merge to make sure docs and changelog reflect what was built.

agents.name: e2e-runner
agents.description: Runs a browser end-to-end suite (Playwright, Cypress, WebdriverIO or Selenium), reproduces each failure, classifies it as a product bug, a flaky test or an environment problem using traces and repeated runs, and repairs only test-side flakiness with a minimal, evidenced diff. Use when an e2e or UI test run is red or intermittently failing locally or in CI and someone needs it triaged and stabilised.

agents.name: fastapi-reviewer
agents.description: FastAPI change auditor that traces each touched route and dependency to catch blocking I/O inside async def handlers, database sessions or clients that are never closed, request models that accept unvalidated or server-owned fields, routes that skip or weaken the auth dependency, and responses that expose private fields because response_model is missing, and reports only findings it has confirmed, read-only. Use when a FastAPI branch, diff or pull request needs a review before it is merged.

agents.name: flutter-reviewer
agents.description: Flutter-specific change reviewer that runs in its own context, reads the diff plus the surrounding widgets, and reports verified defects such as widgets rebuilding far more than needed, BuildContext or setState used after an await without a mounted check, controllers, streams and timers never disposed, futures created in build, and code that breaks on iOS, Android or web. It never edits files. Use when someone wants a Flutter or Dart UI pull request, branch or uncommitted change checked before merging, or suspects a Flutter screen leaks memory, janks or crashes after navigation.

agents.name: fsharp-build-resolver
agents.description: Gets a failing F# build green again by diagnosing compiler errors such as FS0039 from wrong .fsproj compile order, FS0072 and FS0001 type inference failures, FS0030 value restriction, and indentation errors, plus NuGet, FSharp.Core and Paket restore problems, applying the smallest fix and re-running the build to prove it. Use when dotnet build or dotnet test fails to compile an F# project, or package restore breaks for an F# solution.

agents.name: fsharp-reviewer
agents.description: F#-specific change reviewer that hunts for partial functions like List.head and Option.get, exceptions leaking out of Result pipelines, incomplete or wildcard-masked pattern matches, shared mutable state, and nulls arriving from .NET interop, then returns verified findings without editing code. Use when a diff, branch or pull request touches .fs, .fsi or .fsx files and the user wants it checked before merging.

agents.name: go-build-resolver
agents.description: Repair subagent for broken Go builds that diagnoses go build, go vet and compile errors plus module failures (go.mod and go.sum mismatches, replace directives, version conflicts, missing or ambiguous imports, toolchain directives) and applies the smallest fix, then re-runs the failing command to prove it passes. Use when go build, go vet, go test compilation or go mod tidy fails, or a Go dependency upgrade leaves the module unbuildable.

agents.name: go-reviewer
agents.description: Go-specific reviewer subagent that reads a Go diff or package and reports verified defects such as unchecked errors, leaked goroutines, data races, misused context.Context, nil-pointer dereferences, typed-nil interfaces and slice or map aliasing, ranked by severity and without modifying code. Use when the user wants Go changes, a Go pull request or a Go package checked for concurrency and error-handling bugs before merging.

agents.name: infra-reviewer
agents.description: Audits infrastructure files in a separate context, covering Dockerfiles, Compose files, Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts, Terraform or OpenTofu code and plans, and CI pipeline configs, and returns verified findings on security misconfiguration, missing resource limits and probes, state and secret exposure, and plan changes that would replace or destroy live resources, without editing files or applying anything. Use when the user wants infrastructure or deployment config checked before merge or apply, a terraform plan screened for destructive changes, or a container and cluster setup audited for hardening gaps.

agents.name: java-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing Maven and Gradle builds for Java projects, covering javac compile errors, unresolved or conflicting dependency versions, annotation processors such as Lombok and MapStruct, and JDK, toolchain or release-level mismatches, using the smallest edit and re-running the build to prove it passes. Use when mvn or gradle fails to compile, a Java build broke after a dependency or JDK upgrade, or the error mentions NoSuchMethodError, cannot find symbol, or an unsupported class file version.

agents.name: java-reviewer
agents.description: Java-specific code reviewer that inspects a diff for NullPointerException paths, unclosed streams and connections, broken equals/hashCode contracts, data races and lock misuse, swallowed or mis-wrapped exceptions, and misuse of JDK and framework APIs, then returns verified findings without editing files. Use when the user wants a Java or Spring change reviewed before merge, asks whether Java code is thread-safe, or suspects a leak or null bug in a Java pull request.

agents.name: kotlin-build-resolver
agents.description: Gets a failing Kotlin or Gradle build green again with the smallest possible change, diagnosing compiler errors such as unresolved references and type mismatches, kapt and KSP processor failures, Kotlin Gradle plugin, KSP, Compose compiler and AGP version mismatches, JVM target conflicts and dependency resolution conflicts, then re-runs the failing task to prove the fix. Use when ./gradlew build, assemble or compileKotlin fails, a Kotlin version bump broke the build, an annotation processor like Room, Hilt or Moshi stops generating code, or Gradle reports incompatible or conflicting dependency versions.

agents.name: kotlin-reviewer
agents.description: Kotlin-specific change reviewer for JVM and Android projects that hunts for !! crashes, coroutine scope leaks, blocking calls on the main thread, swallowed CancellationException, Flow collected twice or outside the lifecycle, and nullable platform types leaking in from Java, then returns verified, ranked findings without touching files. Use when the user wants a Kotlin diff, branch or pull request reviewed, asks whether their coroutine or Flow code is safe, or wants a second check on Kotlin code that calls Java libraries.

agents.name: mle-reviewer
agents.description: Audits machine learning code in a separate context for data leakage between splits, train and eval behaving differently, metrics that do not measure the stated goal, unseeded or non-reproducible randomness, and silent tensor shape or broadcasting bugs, then returns verified findings without editing files. Use when the user wants ML training, feature or evaluation code checked before trusting a result, merging a model change, or reporting a metric.

agents.name: network-config-reviewer
agents.description: Audits firewall rulesets, router exports, VPN configs and DNS server settings (nftables, iptables, ufw, pf, OPNsense/pfSense XML, OpenWrt, MikroTik, WireGuard, OpenVPN, IPsec, Unbound, BIND, dnsmasq) for services exposed to the internet, allow-any or shadowed rules, weak ciphers and key handling, open resolvers, and changes that would lock the admin out, and returns ranked findings with redacted evidence without applying anything. Use when someone wants a second look at a network or VPN configuration before deploying it, after a change, or when they suspect something is reachable that should not be.

agents.name: payments-reviewer
agents.description: Audits payment and billing code for money-losing defects with any provider (Stripe, Paystack, Flutterwave, M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, Hubtel and others), hunting for prices or amounts trusted from the client, webhooks or callbacks acted on without signature or status verification, missing idempotency on charges and fulfilment, float arithmetic on money, leaked secret keys and unhandled pending, failed or reversed states, then returns a ranked, verified list without editing anything. Use when the user wants checkout, webhook, payout or subscription code checked before release, or asks whether their payment integration can be faked, double-charge or double-fulfil.

agents.name: performance-optimizer
agents.description: Measures a specific slow endpoint, job, query or function with a repeatable benchmark and a profiler, pins down the single biggest cost from evidence rather than guesswork, applies the narrowest fix that removes it, and reports timings before and after. Use when the user says a particular request, page, script, build step or test run is too slow, uses too much memory or CPU, and wants it made faster.

agents.name: perl-build-resolver
agents.description: Fixes broken Perl installs and startup failures - cpanm or Carton dependency errors, XS modules that fail to compile against missing C headers or libraries, and "Can't locate Foo.pm in @INC" load-path problems - with the smallest change, then re-runs the failing command to prove it works. Use when cpanm, carton install, perl Makefile.PL, make or a Perl script fails to build, install or load a module.

agents.name: perl-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for Perl 5 diffs that hunts missing strict or warnings, two-arg open and shell-string system or backtick calls, unanchored or injectable regexes, list-versus-scalar context mistakes, unchecked eval and $@ handling, and SQL or command injection, returning verified findings by severity. Use when someone wants a Perl pull request, .pm module change or .pl script checked for bugs and security holes before merging.

agents.name: php-build-resolver
agents.description: Fix-it subagent for PHP projects that will not install, autoload or pass analysis, resolving Composer dependency conflicts and platform requirement errors, "Class not found" PSR-4 autoload mismatches, PHPStan or Psalm failures, and code broken by a PHP version upgrade, through the smallest edit followed by a re-run of the failing command as proof. Use when composer install or composer update errors out, a PHP class stops autoloading, static analysis turns CI red, or moving to a newer PHP release surfaces deprecations and fatal errors.

agents.name: php-reviewer
agents.description: PHP-focused review subagent that inspects a PHP diff, pull request or directory and returns severity-ranked, verified findings on SQL injection, cross-site scripting, loose-comparison type juggling, files missing declare(strict_types=1), unserialize on untrusted data, swallowed exceptions and unchecked false returns, never changing the code itself. Use when someone wants PHP, Laravel or Symfony changes audited for injection, escaping and error-handling defects before they merge.

agents.name: planner
agents.description: Implementation planning subagent that reads the codebase and turns a feature request or change into an ordered, step-by-step plan naming the exact files to touch, the tests to write first, the risks, and a checkpoint command after each step, all without editing code. Use when the user wants a feature, bug fix or migration broken down before coding starts, asks what files a change will touch, or wants work split into small reviewable steps.

agents.name: pr-test-analyzer
agents.description: Audits the tests that accompany a pull request or branch against the behaviour it changes, mapping each changed branch to the test that covers it, flagging untested cases, assertions too weak to fail and mocks that replace the code under test, and returns a ranked list of specific tests to add, without editing files. Use when someone asks whether a PR is adequately tested, what tests a change still needs, or for a test-quality review before merge.

agents.name: python-build-resolver
agents.description: Diagnoses and repairs broken Python builds and environments with the smallest possible change, covering ModuleNotFoundError and import errors, pip, uv and poetry dependency resolution conflicts, stale lockfiles, pyproject.toml packaging and build-backend failures, mypy or pyright type errors, and wrong-interpreter or virtualenv mix-ups, then re-runs the failing command to prove it passes. Use when a Python install, import, type check or package build is failing and the user wants it fixed rather than explained.

agents.name: python-reviewer
agents.description: Python-specific change reviewer that hunts mutable default arguments, swallowed or over-broad exceptions, missing or wrong type hints, blocking calls and unawaited coroutines in asyncio code, unclosed files and connections, SQL and shell injection, and plain logic bugs, then returns verified findings ranked by severity without touching the code. Use when the user wants a Python diff, branch or pull request checked before merging, or asks whether a Python change is safe.

agents.name: rag-reviewer
agents.description: Audits the code and configuration of a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline (ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector and keyword search, reranking, permission filters, prompt assembly, citations, index freshness and evals) and returns ranked weaknesses, each with a concrete fix, while leaving every file untouched. Use when the user wants a RAG system, semantic search index or chat-over-documents feature reviewed, or asks why retrieval quality is poor before deciding what to change.

agents.name: react-reviewer
agents.description: React and Next.js change reviewer that reads a diff in its own context and reports verified defects - Rules of Hooks violations, effects with missing or wrong dependencies and no cleanup, stale closures, unstable or index keys, state mirrored from props, "use client"/"use server" boundary leaks of secrets or server data, unprotected Server Actions, and accessibility regressions - without editing files. Use when the user wants a React, JSX/TSX or Next.js App Router change, branch or pull request reviewed before merging.

agents.name: refactor-cleaner
agents.description: Removes dead code from a repository, including unreferenced functions and files, unused exports, unused package dependencies and duplicated helper functions, but only after gathering evidence that nothing uses each item, and runs the tests after every single deletion. Use when the user wants to prune dead code, drop unused dependencies, shrink a bloated codebase, or consolidate copy-pasted utility functions.

agents.name: ruby-build-resolver
agents.description: Repair subagent that gets a broken Ruby environment loading again by fixing Bundler resolution conflicts, lockfile platform mismatches, gem native extension compile failures (nokogiri, pg, mysql2, ffi, psych), LoadError and load path problems, and Ruby version mismatches with the smallest possible change, then re-runs the failing command as proof. Use when bundle install or bundle exec fails, a gem will not build its C extension, Ruby raises cannot load such file, or the app refuses to boot after a Ruby or gem upgrade.

agents.name: ruby-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only review subagent for Ruby and Rails diffs that hunts NoMethodError on nil, rescue clauses that swallow everything, N+1 queries and missing eager loading, risky metaprogramming such as send or constantize on user input, unpermitted mass assignment, and SQL, shell or YAML injection, then returns verified findings ranked by severity. Use when the user wants a Ruby branch, pull request or set of changed .rb files checked before merge, or asks whether a Rails change introduces nil crashes, query explosions or injection holes.

agents.name: rust-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing cargo build, cargo check and cargo test compilation by reading rustc error codes and fixing borrow checker conflicts, lifetime mismatches, unsatisfied trait bounds, missing feature flags and conflicting dependency versions with the smallest diff, then re-running cargo to prove the build is green. Use when a Rust project no longer compiles, rustc reports errors such as E0502, E0499, E0382, E0277 or E0308, or a Cargo.lock or dependency upgrade broke the build.

agents.name: rust-reviewer
agents.description: Rust-specific change reviewer that hunts for unwrap and expect outside tests, reachable panics and indexing, unsound or undocumented unsafe blocks, blocking calls and std Mutex guards held across await in tokio code, needless clones, and swallowed or stringly-typed errors, then returns verified findings without touching files. Use when a Rust diff, crate or pull request needs a language-aware review before merge, or when the user wants a second opinion on unsafe or async Rust code.

agents.name: security-reviewer
agents.description: Isolated security pass over a diff, branch or pull request that traces untrusted input to where it is used and reports only exploitable problems - leaked secrets, SQL, shell and template injection, path traversal and SSRF, missing or broken authorization (IDOR), weak input validation, and sensitive data in responses or logs - each ranked by severity with an attack scenario and a fix, never modifying the code. Use when the user wants a vulnerability check of their change delegated to a subagent, a security gate before merging, or an independent look at whether a new endpoint or handler can be abused.

agents.name: silent-failure-hunter
agents.description: Read-only auditor that searches a diff, module or service for places where failures vanish without a trace, such as empty or catch-all exception handlers, discarded error returns, unawaited promises, fallback values that mask a broken dependency, and error paths with no log or metric, then reports each with its concrete consequence. Use when the user suspects errors are being hidden, asks why something fails with no logs, or wants a change audited for swallowed exceptions before merging.

agents.name: swift-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing Swift and Xcode builds with the smallest diff, working through compiler errors, Swift 6 strict concurrency diagnostics such as non-Sendable sends and actor-isolated access, SwiftPM dependency resolution and Package.resolved conflicts, and build settings like SWIFT_VERSION or search paths, then re-runs the failing build to prove it passes. Use when swift build, swift test or xcodebuild fails, after a toolchain, Xcode or Swift 6 upgrade breaks compilation, or when SwiftPM cannot resolve or fetch packages. Not for code signing or provisioning problems.

agents.name: swift-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only Swift code reviewer that inspects a diff for crash-prone force unwraps and try!, retain cycles in escaping closures, actor isolation mistakes and Sendable violations, UIKit or SwiftUI state touched off the main actor, and swallowed or misrouted errors, then returns verified findings ranked by severity. Use when the user wants a Swift or iOS/macOS pull request checked before merge, asks whether a change could leak memory or race, or wants a second opinion on Swift concurrency code.

agents.name: typescript-build-resolver
agents.description: Repairs failing TypeScript and JavaScript builds with the smallest diff, working through tsc type errors, "Cannot find module" and module resolution failures, ESM/CJS interop errors, bundler (Vite, webpack, esbuild, tsup) failures and broken or mismatched npm/pnpm dependencies, then re-runs the failing command to prove it passes. Use when tsc, npm run build, a bundler or CI type-check is red and the user wants it green again.

agents.name: typescript-reviewer
agents.description: TypeScript and JavaScript diff reviewer that hunts type holes (any, unsafe casts, non-null assertions, ts-ignore), floating or unhandled promises, async races, ESM/CommonJS import breakage and runtime bugs the compiler cannot see, then returns verified findings without touching files. Use when a TS/JS change, branch or pull request needs a language-aware review before it is committed or merged.

agents.name: vue-reviewer
agents.description: Read-only reviewer for Vue 3 and Nuxt diffs that hunts for state which silently stops being reactive, watchers and listeners never torn down, props or store state mutated from a child, server and client rendering that disagree, and Nuxt data fetched twice or secrets exposed through public runtime config, then returns verified findings with file and line. Use when the user wants a Vue or Nuxt pull request, branch or uncommitted change checked before merge.

commands.name: build-fix
commands.description: Fix the current build, compile or type-check failure with the smallest change, routed to the build resolver for that language.

commands.name: commit
commands.description: Write a Conventional Commits message for the staged changes, show it, and commit only after the user confirms.

commands.name: onboard
commands.description: Get oriented in an unfamiliar codebase: what it does, how it is laid out, how to build, test and run it, and where to start.

commands.name: plan-feature
commands.description: Turn a feature request into a step-by-step implementation plan with files to touch, risks and tests, without writing code.

commands.name: pr-describe
commands.description: Draft a pull request title and description for the current branch from its commits and diff against the base branch.

commands.name: refactor-clean
commands.description: Find and remove dead code, unused exports and unused dependencies, verifying with the build and tests after each removal.

commands.name: resume-session
commands.description: Resume work from the latest session handoff note, checking it against the repository before taking the next step.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review the current changes for bugs, risky patterns and missing tests, routed to the reviewer for the language that changed.

commands.name: save-session
commands.description: Save a handoff note recording the current goal, progress, decisions and next steps so a later session can resume.

commands.name: security-scan
commands.description: Scan the current change for vulnerabilities, leaked secrets and unsafe dependencies, and report findings by severity.

commands.name: test-coverage
commands.description: Find untested behaviour in the current change and add focused tests for it, then show the coverage before and after.

commands.name: update-docs
commands.description: Update the README, API docs, changelog and code comments that the current change made stale, without touching unrelated docs.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify the current changes by running the project's build, lint, type-check and tests, then report pass or fail.

hooks.name: block-dangerous-commands
hooks.description: Stops the agent before it runs shell commands that destroy data or systems, such as rm -rf on / or your home folder, force-pushing main, wiping disks, piping curl into a shell, dropping databases or auto-approved terraform destroy.

hooks.name: block-no-verify
hooks.description: Stops the agent from skipping the project's git hooks with git commit --no-verify, -n, HUSKY=0, SKIP= or a swapped core.hooksPath, so pre-commit checks keep running.

hooks.name: format-on-edit
hooks.description: After the agent edits a file, formats it with the formatter the project already uses (Biome or Prettier, Ruff or Black, gofmt, rustfmt), so agent changes match the project's style.

hooks.name: guard-secrets
hooks.description: Stops the agent from writing API keys, tokens, passwords, connection strings or private keys into files, using the same rules as the security-review secret scanner.

hooks.name: load-session-context
hooks.description: At the start of each session, tells the agent the current branch, how many uncommitted changes there are, and the latest session handoff note, so it picks up where the last session stopped.

hooks.name: protect-files
hooks.description: Stops the agent from editing files that should never be hand-edited, such as .env files with secrets, package lockfiles, anything inside .git, and private keys.
